title: 5 Batteries-Included Web Frameworks Worth Knowing
summary: Compare five batteries-included web frameworks—Rails, Django, Laravel, Phoenix, and Loco—by built-in features, standout strengths, and the teams each suits.
body_markdown:
A batteries-included web framework ships routing, an ORM with database migrations, authentication, background jobs, email and a testing setup as one coordinated package, so a team configures defaults instead of choosing and wiring separate libraries.


If you build with Express or Next.js, you know how this usually goes. The feature is a password reset email, but first you spend a week comparing ORMs, queue libraries and mailers, and then you discover the auth library doesn’t work with your session store.


This article covers five frameworks in five languages that ship those pieces for you: Rails, Django, Laravel, Phoenix and Loco. For each one you get the language, what’s in the box, what it’s known for and who it suits, judged on the same criteria.


## Key Takeaways


- A batteries-included framework gives you routing, ORM, migrations, auth, jobs, mail and testing in one release, so they are documented and upgraded together.
- The trade-off is coupling: the faster a framework gets you to a working feature, the more your app depends on its conventions and upgrade path.
- Since Rails 8.0, Rails ships a built-in authentication generator, and Solid Queue is the default Active Job backend for new apps.
- Since Django 6.0, core includes a Tasks framework for queuing background work, but production execution needs a third-party worker backend.
- Phoenix’s` mix phx.gen.auth` generates email-based authentication with magic-link login by default, and Loco brings the Rails model to Rust on top of Axum and SeaORM.


## What Is a Batteries-Included Framework?


A batteries-included framework treats the standard backend layers as part of the framework rather than as add-ons. You get routing, data access and migrations, authentication, a job queue, a mailer and a test harness, all built to work together, with generators that produce code using every layer.


Coming from Express, the difference is this: you would normally pick an ORM such as Prisma, a queue such as BullMQ, an auth library and a mailer, then wire them up and upgrade them one by one. In a batteries-included framework, all of those come from one project. They share one set of docs and generators and get upgraded together in a single release. JavaScript has its own options here. AdonisJS is the closest to this model, covered in[our look at Rails-style JavaScript frameworks](https://blog.openreplay.com/rails-javascript/) . NestJS focuses on application structure rather than bundling every layer.


Batteries-included frameworks suit teams whose main constraint is shipping features. They suit teams least when requirements regularly cut against the framework’s assumptions about data, authentication or deployment. They are also a poor fit for teams that want to swap individual layers, and for services small enough that a router plus one library covers everything. Some ecosystems prefer composing small libraries by culture. Go is the usual example, as covered in[our guide to Go web frameworks](https://blog.openreplay.com/best-go-web-frameworks-scalable-applications/) .


Coupling is the cost of a batteries-included framework. Defaults that speed up the first release also tie your business logic to the framework’s conventions, which matters when it is time to upgrade or test in isolation.


## Ruby on Rails


Rails is the Ruby framework that made convention over configuration mainstream. It is the reference point for the other four. Rails 8.1 is the current release series, and the latest patch is[Rails 8.1.4](https://rubyonrails.org/2026/9/24/Rails-Version-8-1-4-has-been-released) .


**In the box:** routing, Active Record with migrations, Action Mailer, Active Job and a default test framework. Starting with version 8.0, Rails comes with a[default authentication generator](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/security.html) , which adds the models, controllers, views, routes and migrations for basic login and password reset. For jobs,[Solid Queue is the Active Job default](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_job_basics.html) in new apps. It is backed by the database, so you don’t need Redis.


**Known for:** generators and conventions. If files, classes and tables follow the expected names, routing and model mapping work with almost no setup.


```text
bin/rails   generate   scaffold   Post   title:string   body:text
```


The Rails scaffold command generates a model, a migration, a controller, views, routes and tests for a full CRUD resource.


**Suits:** small teams that want the deepest convention-driven workflow and are happy to accept Rails’ opinions.


## Django


Django is Python’s batteries-included framework. Its standout feature is an admin interface generated from your models. The Django team[announced the release of Django 6.1](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/aug/05/django-61-released/) in August 2026.


**In the box:** URL routing, an ORM that generates migrations from model changes,` django.contrib.auth` , an email API and a test framework. Since[Django 6.0, core includes a Tasks framework](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.0/releases/6.0/) (` django.tasks` ) for defining and queuing background tasks. Its built-in backends are for development and testing, so running tasks in production needs a separate third-party worker backend.


**Known for:** the[Django admin site](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.1/ref/contrib/admin/) , which builds a working back-office interface from your model definitions. A stack you assemble from separate libraries doesn’t give you that.


```text
python   manage.py   startapp   blog
```


Django’s` startapp` command creates an app package with modules for models, views, admin registration, tests and migrations. Django core has no CRUD scaffold generator.


**Suits:** teams already working in Python, and apps that need internal admin tooling from day one.


## Laravel


Laravel is the PHP framework with the widest first-party ecosystem of the five.[Laravel 13](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/releases) is the current major version.


**In the box:** Laravel bundles routing, the Eloquent ORM with migrations, a[queue system](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/queues) , mail, the Blade templating engine, the Artisan CLI and testing in one framework. Official[starter kits](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/starter-kits) scaffold authentication, and first-party packages such as Echo cover real-time broadcasting on the client.


**Known for:** an API surface where queues, mail and the database read like one library, plus a large set of official packages for whatever falls outside core.


```text
php   artisan   make:model   Post   --migration   --controller   --resource
```


Laravel’s` make:model` command with these flags creates an[Eloquent model](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/eloquent) with a matching migration and a resource controller.


**Suits:** teams that want widely available PHP hosting and prefer official packages over picking from the community.


## Phoenix


Phoenix brings the batteries-included approach to Elixir. It combines generators and the Ecto database library with LiveView, which builds interactive, server-rendered interfaces.[Phoenix 1.8](https://www.phoenixframework.org/blog/phoenix-1-8-released) is the current release.


**In the box:** routing, Ecto schemas and migrations, Channels and PubSub, and[mix phx.gen.auth](https://hexdocs.pm/phoenix/mix_phx_gen_auth.html) . That generator produces email-based authentication with magic-link login by default and passwords as an option, built on LiveView by default. Phoenix’s standout is[LiveView](https://hexdocs.pm/phoenix_live_view/) .


```text
mix   phx.gen.html   Blog   Post   posts   title:string   body:text
```


Phoenix’s` mix phx.gen.html` command[generates a context, schema, migration, controller, templates and tests](https://hexdocs.pm/phoenix/Mix.Tasks.Phx.Gen.Html.html) .


**Suits:** real-time products where you would rather not maintain a separate SPA.


## Loco


Loco is a Rails-inspired framework for Rust, built on Axum, with models and migrations powered by SeaORM. The[project homepage](https://loco.rs/) describes it as batteries-included Rust, at v1.2.0.


**In the box:** the Loco homepage lists models, controllers, jobs, mailers and auth, all generated and wired together. Authentication is JWT-based.


```text
cargo   loco   generate   scaffold   post   title:string   content:text
```


According to the[Loco generator docs](https://loco.rs/docs/how-to/use-generators/) , Loco’s scaffold command creates a model, a migration, request and response types, a JSON API controller with routes, and a model test. Scaffolded routes require JWT auth unless you pass` --no-auth` .


**Suits:** teams that want a compiled, typed Rust backend and the Rails workflow together.


## How Do You Choose a Batteries-Included Framework?


Start with the language your team already knows, then use the standout feature to break a tie. Pick Django for a free admin interface. Pick Rails for convention-driven generators. Pick Laravel for first-party packages and easy hosting. Pick Phoenix for real-time server-rendered UI, and Loco for Rust with the same model. Before you commit, run the one generator command for your shortlisted framework against a real feature from your backlog, and check how much code you’d write beyond what it gives you.


## FAQs


Does Django's built-in Tasks framework replace Celery?


Not entirely. The django.tasks module added in Django 6.0 handles defining, validating and queuing tasks and storing their results, but it does not ship a worker. Its built-in ImmediateBackend and DummyBackend are meant for development and testing. In production you install a third-party backend that provides a durable queue and a worker process, and run that worker separately. Celery is still the stronger fit for tasks that depend on one another.


Can I use Rails or Laravel as an API-only backend for a React or Next.js frontend?


Yes. Running rails new my_api --api gives you a smaller middleware stack and makes ApplicationController inherit from ActionController::API. It also stops generators from creating views, helpers and assets, so scaffolds render JSON. Since Laravel 11, php artisan install:api creates routes/api.php and installs Laravel Sanctum, which handles token authentication for SPAs and mobile clients.


Is there a batteries-included framework for Node.js?


AdonisJS is the closest Node.js equivalent. It is a TypeScript framework that ships authentication, an ORM, validation, mail, queues, caching and testing as parts built to work together. Its data layer is Lucid, an Active Record ORM built on Knex that includes migrations. Testing runs on Japa, a test framework from the same team. Authentication supports sessions for web apps and access tokens for APIs.
